request: Please find me data regarding first-of-class ship cost overruns

reply.reply:
**CRS reports show lead-ship cost exposure across Navy programs: the lead carrier’s final procurement cost was $13,316.5 million, and a frigate lead ship was estimated at $1,499.3 million; separate Columbia reporting identifies cost-growth risk.**

- The lead ship had an estimated procurement cost of $1,499.3 million, above follow-on ships due to learning-curve position and included design/nonrecurring engineering costs. (R44972, PDF p. 10)
- CBO estimates the 10 Columbia submarines following the first two will average $9.4 billion each, $1.5 billion more than the Navy estimate. (R41129, PDF p. 17)
- GAO found lead Columbia submarine cost and schedule performance consistently missed targets through early 2024, with future risks likely adding to cost and schedule growth. (R41129, PDF p. 17)
- The ship’s final procurement cost was $13,316.5 million in then-year dollars. (RS20643, PDF p. 7)
reply.reasoning: The evidence provides two lead-ship procurement costs and separate Columbia cost-growth evidence, but not directly comparable original-versus-final overrun calculations.
